clips.title: Proxy vs Reverse Proxy (Real-world Examples)
clips.why: A clear picture of a forward proxy: a machine that sends requests out on behalf of others and can refuse the ones it does not allow.
look: The clients talk only to the proxy; the proxy talks to the internet.
A forward proxy is where an organization blocks sites.
The proxy is a separate machine from the clients.
clips.after: Our egress proxy is a forward proxy on its own machines, which is exactly why root on a sandbox cannot change its list.

clips.title: Transition to IMDSv2 on EC2 - Introduction, Preparation, Pitfalls
clips.why: A demo of how something running on a machine reaches the metadata service and walks away with the machine's credentials.
look: How the credentials are fetched from the metadata address.
What IMDSv2's token and hop limit change in the demo.
That anything running on the machine as root can still get them.
clips.after: That is why our launch template requires tokens with hop limit 1 and, more importantly, gives the VM a role that is worth almost nothing.

practice.q: Complete the launch template line that stops containers on the VM from getting a metadata token.
practice.hint: How many network hops the token answer may travel.
practice.why: With one hop, the answer reaches a process on the VM but not a container behind Docker's network.

practice.q: In the lab, root unset HTTPS_PROXY and curl said "Could not resolve host". Which wall stopped it?

options.text: The network with no route out
options.why: Without the proxy there is no road at all; even the name lookup has nowhere to go.
The request never reached the proxy once the variable was gone.
That rule only covers the metadata address, and root could delete it anyway.

practice.q: Put the attacker's attempt from the story in order, with the wall that finally stops it.
items: Start a container with the host's disk mounted and become root
Delete the iptables rule and read the role from the metadata service
Find that the role allows almost nothing
Unset HTTPS_PROXY and try to upload directly
Fail, because the network has no route out and the proxy refuses every site but the mirror
practice.why: Every inside rule falls to root, and every outside wall still holds.

practice.q: Which size of sandbox VM does Nova use for planning, and why not the big one?

options.text: lite (m8i.xlarge), because planning only reads code and an approved plan is what pays for a full VM
options.why: Planning is cheap work; the full size is claimed only after a person approves the plan.
Planning waits on the model, not the CPU. A wide VM would cost more for nothing.

options.text: Any size, because all three use different images
options.why: All three use the same image; only the instance type differs.
